en.content:
Hong Kong’s public consultation on its first five-year plan is being framed as a chance to accelerate sustainability, and there is reason to be cautiously optimistic. After years of episodic policy measures, a structured roadmap can convert broad commitments into clearer targets—such as emissions reduction, waste management, and energy efficiency—while also clarifying how different bureaus will coordinate delivery. In principle, this is the kind of “whole-of-government” planning that can help reduce policy fragmentation and give both the public and industry more predictability.

Yet consultation should not become a ritual of collecting opinions that later disappear into the fine print. Sustainability in Hong Kong is inseparable from land constraints, the city’s dense built environment, and the costs of transitioning supply chains and transport patterns. The test of the plan will therefore be whether the government translates public input into measurable benchmarks, timelines, and budgeting priorities that can withstand political cycles. Citizens and stakeholders will understandably ask: what will be delivered in the first two years, and how will progress be reported in a way that is publicly verifiable?

At the same time, the consultation offers an opportunity to set expectations about practical trade-offs, including affordability and competitiveness. A credible plan should articulate how Hong Kong can decarbonise without undermining livelihoods or worsening the burden on small businesses. It should also recognise that sustainability is not only about environmental outcomes, but about resilience—preparing the city for extreme weather, public health pressures, and supply disruptions. When the plan speaks to these realities, it can move beyond slogans and win broader buy-in.

Ultimately, a five-year plan is most valuable when it becomes a living contract between authorities and society, not merely a document for announcements. If the consultation results in clear, enforceable goals—paired with public reporting and periodic adjustments—Hong Kong can strengthen its sustainability governance while reinforcing social trust in how policy is made and followed through.
en.topic_title: Public consultation for Hong Kong’s 5-year plan offers golden chance to step up city’s sustainability game

zh.content:
香港正踏入一個「睇得見」同「做得到」嘅關鍵節點。行政長官正展開五年計劃公眾諮詢，表面係政策程序，實際上係一場城市方向嘅再校準：點樣喺經濟壓力、人口結構變化同社會期望之間，重新定義可持續發展嘅優先次序。若諮詢真係做到「聆聽—量化—落地」，就唔應該只停留喺語氣正確嘅口號，而係要用清晰指標去追蹤成效，例如減碳路徑、能源轉型進度、廢物管理效率、綠色基建回報與公私營協作機制等。

不過，真正考驗喺落地，而唔喺參與本身。過往社會最擔心嘅，係諮詢變成「收意見、無方向」，或者一切最後都回到單一部門、單一預算、單一時間表；而可持續其實跨越運輸、土地、環境、產業同民生，牽涉協同成本同政治取捨。五年計劃必須講清楚取捨：例如交通政策係要以公共運輸、步行與電動化為主，定係繼續用短期紓緩去拖延結構改革；城市更新係偏向「修補式」維修，定係走向低碳建築、再用再循環物料嘅系統性轉型。只有咁，市民先會相信參與唔係象徵。

同時，香港要避免「可持續」被狹義化成環保活動或形象工程。真正嘅可持續包括韌性：極端天氣、供應鏈波動、以及公共衛生與基建安全，都要納入風險管理框架。單靠技術改善唔夠，亦要處理社會公平——例如在減碳及節能上，成本應該點分擔、補貼機制點設計，先至唔會令轉型變成某些階層嘅額外負擔。政策若能把「環境效益」同「生活改善」綁定，例如空氣質素、熱島效應、交通時間可靠度同社區公共空間質素，公眾諮詢就會由程序變成共同承擔。

我認為，香港要把呢次五年計劃諮詢做成一個「可核實嘅承諾」。政府應公開：目標、里程碑、資源安排、跨部門責任分工、以及未能達標時嘅補救方案；亦要引入第三方評估，避免自我檢討「越講越漂亮但越做越散」。只要能夠以可衡量指標建立信任，香港就有機會把可持續變成城市競爭力，而唔係只得口號。否則，下一輪諮詢仍會淪為同一個循環：市民感到參與無果、政府感到執行無阻、但城市面對嘅環境與社會壓力卻只會遞增。
